model.en: The colour scale covers pH 0–14. Real samples can fall outside this range. Neutral means [H⁺] = [OH⁻]. Neutral pH is 7 at 25 °C and changes with temperature.
model.ru: Шкала цветов охватывает pH 0–14. Реальные образцы могут выходить за этот диапазон. Нейтральный раствор — тот, в котором [H⁺] = [OH⁻]. pH нейтрального раствора равен 7 при 25 °C и меняется с температурой.

atomBuilder.title: Atom Builder
atomBuilder.description: Move the slider to choose Z from 1 to 20. The builder shows a neutral atom of one example isotope: protons (Z), neutrons (A − Z), electrons (equal to Z) and electron shells. Electron paths are not shown.
atomBuilder.shellNote: Each number is the count of electrons in one shell, counted from the nucleus outwards. The numbers add up to Z. Potassium (Z = 19) has 2,8,8,1: one electron is already in the fourth shell, although the third shell can take 18 and has only 8.

contrast.en: “Neutral” means the atom’s charge is zero, not that it has no neutrons. Neutrons have no charge, so they do not affect the balance of protons and electrons.
contrast.ru: «Нейтральный» значит, что заряд атома равен нулю, а не что в нём нет нейтронов. Нейтроны не имеют заряда, поэтому на равенство числа протонов и электронов они не влияют.

model.en: It applies to isolated neutral atoms of the first 20 elements in the ground state. It does not show bonding or ions. It cannot give relative atomic mass: that needs the abundance of every isotope, but the constructor shows one example isotope.
model.ru: Модель применима к отдельным нейтральным атомам первых 20 элементов в основном состоянии (ground state). Она не показывает химические связи и ионы. Относительную атомную массу (relative atomic mass) по ней не найти: для неё нужна доля каждого изотопа в природе, а конструктор показывает один пример изотопа.

moleCalc.title: Mole Calculator
moleCalc.description: Enter a number and choose a conversion direction. Molar mass M links mass and amount of substance. Molar volume Vm links amount of substance and gas volume.
moleCalc.stpNote: Gas volumes here use STP: 0 °C, 273 K, 100 kPa, where Vm = 22.7 dm³/mol. Normal conditions (0 °C, 101.325 kPa) give Vm = 22.4 dm³/mol, so do not mix the two values.
moleCalc.invalidInput: Enter a number that is zero or more. Mass conversions also need a molar mass greater than zero.

contrast.en: The volume here is a gas volume. Do not enter the volume of a solution: for solutions, use concentration instead.
contrast.ru: Здесь объём — это объём газа. Объём раствора сюда не вводи: для растворов используй концентрацию.

energyProfile.title: Energy profile of a reaction
energyProfile.description: Compare the enthalpy levels of the reactants and the products. The peak is higher than both the reactants and the products. The gap between the two levels is |ΔH|, the size of the enthalpy change at constant pressure. The horizontal axis shows reaction progress, not time.
energyProfile.exoSummary: the products are lower than the reactants, so the gap between the two levels equals the heat released.
energyProfile.endoSummary: the products are higher than the reactants, so the gap between the two levels equals the heat absorbed.
energyProfile.catalystNote: A catalyst lowers the energy barrier (Eₐ) by the same amount for the forward and the reverse reaction. It does not change ΔH.

contrast.en: The slider sets |ΔH|, the size of the enthalpy change, which is always positive. The diagram shows the same value with a sign: ΔH = −60 kJ/mol if the products are lower, or ΔH = +60 kJ/mol if they are higher.
contrast.ru: Ползунок задаёт модуль |ΔH| — изменение энтальпии без учёта знака, оно всегда положительно. На диаграмме то же число записано со знаком: ΔH = −60 кДж/моль, если продукты ниже реагентов, или ΔH = +60 кДж/моль, если они выше.

atmosphere.title: The Atmosphere
atmosphere.intro: How the atmosphere formed, what dry air is made of, and how its gases affect climate and health.

history.title: History of the atmosphere
history.body: The early atmosphere had almost no oxygen. Its gases probably came from volcanic outgassing and from reactions with rocks. Later, photosynthesis by early organisms released oxygen, which slowly built up in the air. Evidence from that time is scarce: the early air has not survived, and the oldest rocks have changed over time. Today's dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.9% argon and 0.04% carbon dioxide.

contrast.en: Dry air means air without water vapour. The amount of water vapour varies from place to place, so the percentages in this section apply only to dry air.
contrast.ru: Сухой воздух — это воздух без водяного пара. Количество пара меняется от места к месту, поэтому приведённые здесь проценты относятся только к сухому воздуху.

sources.title: БРЭ «Атмосфера Земли»
sources.section: Состав и история атмосферы

carbonRocks.title: Carbon stored in rocks
carbonRocks.body: Carbon is stored in carbonate rocks, such as limestone (CaCO₃), and in fossil fuels. Many marine organisms build shells and skeletons from calcium carbonate. When these remains are buried and compressed, they can form limestone, which holds carbon for a very long time. The ocean also takes up CO₂ from the air and converts part of it into carbonates. Fossil fuels are another carbon store: they formed from ancient organic matter that was buried.

contrast.en: Limestone is not a fuel. Its carbon is bound in carbonate, which does not burn, whereas coal and oil burn and release CO₂.
contrast.ru: Известняк — не топливо. Его углерод связан в карбонатах, которые не горят, а уголь и нефть горят и выделяют CO₂.

sources.section: Углерод в горных породах и круговорот углерода

greenhouse.title: Greenhouse effect
greenhouse.body: The greenhouse effect is the warming of Earth's surface caused by gases that absorb and re-emit infrared radiation. Sunlight heats the surface, which gives off heat as infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases absorb part of this radiation and re-emit it in all directions, so some energy returns to the surface. The main greenhouse gases are water vapour, carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O) and ozone (O₃). When these gases increase, more energy is trapped, so less escapes to space and the surface warms.

contrast.en: The name misleads. A glass greenhouse stays warm mainly because it stops warm air from escaping upwards; the atmospheric effect works through infrared radiation.
contrast.ru: Название вводит в заблуждение. Стеклянная теплица нагревается в основном потому, что не даёт тёплому воздуху уходить вверх; парниковый эффект в атмосфере работает через инфракрасное излучение.

items.cause: Climate change is mainly driven by human emissions, which nature cannot absorb fast enough.
items.evidence: Long-term measurements record the warming, and calculations show that people caused it.
items.consequences: Heat, changing rainfall and rising sea levels hit ecosystems and people unevenly.
items.mitigation: Mitigation tackles the cause, so the warming slows over time.

cause.name: Causes of human-driven climate change
cause.rule: Human-driven climate change is change caused by human activity, mainly by rising concentrations of greenhouse gases. Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests add CO₂ beyond the natural carbon cycle. Agriculture and landfill sites produce mainly methane and nitrous oxide. These gases absorb infrared radiation from the surface, so Earth warms as their concentrations rise. Methane traps more heat per molecule but breaks down within years, while CO₂ stays in the air for centuries.
examples: Most of the carbon from petrol burned in a car engine leaves the exhaust as CO₂.
cause.tip: If a question asks you to state causes, give two or three human activities and name the gas for each.

contrast.en: Past natural climate change and today's change are different things. Climate has changed in the past for natural reasons, but the recent rise in CO₂ matches the burning of fossil fuels.
contrast.ru: Прошлые природные изменения климата и нынешние — разные вещи. Климат менялся и раньше по природным причинам, но недавний рост CO₂ совпадает с сжиганием ископаемого топлива.

sources.title: БРЭ «Климат»
sources.section: Климат и изменение климата

evidence.name: Evidence that the climate is changing
evidence.rule:
Evidence of climate change comes from long-term records of air and ocean temperature, sea level, glacier retreat and CO₂ in the air.

Scientists test the causes by comparing these observations with physical models. Models that leave out human emissions cannot reproduce the warming of recent decades.

Projections of future change are less certain. They depend on climate models and on emission scenarios (how much greenhouse gas people will release). Uncertainty also comes from the ocean, which absorbs heat, and from clouds, which can both cool and warm the planet.
examples: CO₂ in the air was about 280 ppm before the industrial era and is more than 400 ppm today.
evidence.tip: Give the year, region and measure when you use climate statistics.

contrast.en: Weather and climate are different things. Weather is the state of the air over hours or days. Climate is the average pattern of weather over many years.
contrast.ru: Погода и климат — разные вещи. Погода — состояние воздуха за часы или дни. Климат — средний многолетний режим погоды.

sources.title: БРЭ «Климат»
sources.section: Климат и изменение климата

consequences.name: Consequences for ecosystems and people
consequences.rule: Consequences are the effects of climate change on ecosystems and people. The harm depends on the hazard and on exposure, meaning how many people, homes or species are in its path. Vulnerability, meaning how poorly people or ecosystems can cope, also decides the damage. So the same hazard can cause very different damage in different places.
examples: Rising sea levels raise the flood risk for homes on low-lying coasts.
consequences.watchOut: Sea ice already floats on the water, so melting it adds little to sea level. Most of the rise comes from melting glaciers on land and from warmer water expanding.
consequences.tip: For a 'describe' question, give a detailed account: the effect, how it harms and who suffers from it, for example coastal towns during a flood.

contrast.en: Ocean acidification and warming are different processes. Acidification happens when dissolved CO₂ forms a weak acid in seawater and lowers the pH. Warming is caused by greenhouse gases that trap heat near the surface.
contrast.ru: Подкисление океана и потепление — разные процессы. Подкисление — химическая реакция: растворённый в морской воде CO₂ образует слабую кислоту и снижает pH. Потепление же вызывают парниковые газы, которые удерживают тепло у поверхности.

sources.title: БРЭ «Климат»
sources.section: Климат и изменение климата

mitigation.name: Mitigation — reducing emissions
mitigation.rule: Mitigation means cutting greenhouse-gas emissions or increasing their removal from the air. Fewer emissions mean less CO₂ builds up in the air. Removal happens, for example, when growing forests take up CO₂ by photosynthesis.
examples: Replacing a coal power station with wind or solar generation cuts CO₂ emissions for the same amount of electricity.
mitigation.tip: For an 'evaluate' question, compare options by emissions, cost and effects on nature; one criterion is not enough.

contrast.en: Low-carbon and renewable are not the same thing. Nuclear power emits little CO₂ when it runs, but uranium is a finite resource, so it is usually classed as non-renewable. Wind and solar power are both low-carbon and renewable.
contrast.ru: Низкоуглеродный и возобновляемый (renewable) — не одно и то же. Ядерная энергия почти не выбрасывает CO₂ при работе, но уран — ограниченный ресурс, поэтому её обычно относят к невозобновляемой. Ветер и солнце одновременно низкоуглеродны и возобновляемы.

sources.title: БРЭ «Климат»
sources.section: Климат и изменение климата

adaptation.name: Adaptation — living with changing climate
adaptation.rule: Adaptation means adjusting to actual or expected effects of climate change to reduce harm or make use of new opportunities. It lowers the vulnerability of people and ecosystems to these effects.
examples: A city builds drainage channels and a park that can flood, so fewer homes flood in heavy rain.
adaptation.tip: For each adaptation measure, name the hazard it protects against, such as flooding, heat or drought.

contrast.en: Mitigation and adaptation are different responses to warming. Mitigation acts on the cause by cutting emissions, while adaptation acts on the harm and leaves emissions unchanged.
contrast.ru: Смягчение изменения климата и адаптация — разные ответы на потепление. Смягчение изменения климата действует на причину: сокращает выбросы. Адаптация снижает вред, но выбросы не сокращает.

sources.title: БРЭ «Климат»
sources.section: Климат и изменение климата

items.co2: Carbon dioxide is a normal part of clean air, so it counts as a pollutant only because of its amount. Too much of it changes the climate.
items.co: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a poisonous gas. It comes from incomplete burning and reduces the amount of oxygen the blood can carry.
items.soot: Soot and other particulate matter are tiny solid pieces or droplets in the air. They irritate the airways and the lungs.
items.sox: Sulfur dioxide comes from sulfur in coal and oil. Its products make rain acidic.
items.nox: Nitrogen oxides (NOx) come mainly from hot engines and power stations. In sunlight, they help form photochemical smog.

co2.name: Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
co2.rule: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a colourless gas produced by respiration and by complete combustion. Burning fuel releases extra CO₂ into the air. This strengthens the greenhouse effect, so the planet warms.
examples: Propane, a fuel gas, burns completely: C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(g). One propane molecule makes three CO₂ molecules.
co2.tip: When you balance a combustion equation, count carbon first, then hydrogen, and balance oxygen last. Then add the state symbols.

contrast.en: The greenhouse effect, which is a process, and CO₂ are different things: CO₂ is one of the gases that take part in it.
contrast.ru: Парниковый эффект (процесс) и CO₂ — разные понятия: CO₂ — один из газов, которые участвуют в нём.

co.name: Carbon monoxide (CO)
co.rule: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas. It forms when fuel burns with too little oxygen, so the carbon is not fully oxidised to CO₂. In the blood, CO binds to haemoglobin much more strongly than oxygen does. Less oxygen then reaches the body's cells.
examples: A gas heater used in a closed room with blocked vents can form CO. One possible reaction for propane is 2C₃H₈(g) + 7O₂(g) → 6CO(g) + 8H₂O(g).
co.watchOut: Carbon monoxide has no colour and no smell, so people cannot notice it. That is why homes with gas appliances have CO alarms.
co.tip: For 'state', give the source and the type of substance. For 'describe', add the mechanism of harm: binding to haemoglobin.

contrast.en: CO and CO₂ differ by one oxygen atom. CO is a poison, while CO₂ harms mainly through climate change.
contrast.ru: CO и CO₂ отличаются одним атомом кислорода. CO — яд, а CO₂ вредит в основном через изменение климата.

sources.title: US EPA — Carbon Monoxide Basics
sources.section: What is CO? What are the harmful effects of CO?

soot.name: Particulates (soot, PM2.5, PM10)
soot.rule: Particulate matter is a mixture of small solid particles and liquid droplets in the air. Soot is its carbon-rich part, formed in incomplete combustion. PM10 and PM2.5 are size classes based on aerodynamic diameter. Small particles can be breathed in and reach deep into the lungs. Dark soot also absorbs sunlight, which warms the air.
examples: A diesel lorry and a bonfire both release soot particles into the air.
soot.tip: PM2.5 names a size class of particles. Do not read the 2.5 as a percentage of the particles.

contrast.en: Soot is not a gas. It is made of solid particles, while CO, SO₂ and NOx are gases.
contrast.ru: Сажа — не газ: она состоит из твёрдых частиц, а CO, SO₂ и NOx — газы.

sources.title: US EPA — Particulate Matter Basics
sources.section: What is PM? Sources of PM; harmful effects

sox.name: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂)
sox.rule: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is a gas. It forms when sulfur in fuel burns: S(s) + O₂(g) → SO₂(g). In the air, SO₂ is oxidised and reacts with water to form sulfuric acid. This acid falls as acid rain, which harms lakes, forests and buildings.
examples: A coal power station without flue-gas cleaning sends SO₂ up its chimney.

contrast.en: Acid rain is not sulfur dioxide itself. It is the acid made from SO₂ once it reacts in the air.
contrast.ru: Кислотный дождь — это не сам диоксид серы, а кислота, которая из него образуется в воздухе.

sources.title: US EPA — Sulfur Dioxide Basics
sources.section: Sources of SO₂; health and environmental effects

nox.name: Nitrogen oxides (NOx)
nox.rule: Nitrogen oxides (NOx) are mainly NO and NO₂. In the air, NO reacts with more oxygen to form NO₂. NO₂ dissolves in rain water and forms nitric acid, so it contributes to acid rain.
examples: Nitrogen and oxygen react in a car engine at high temperature: N₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO(g).
nox.watchOut: Ozone (O₃) at ground level is harmful: it irritates the lungs and damages plants. The same gas in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV radiation.
nox.tip: If a question asks you to suggest something, name a way to cut NOx, such as a catalytic converter in the exhaust.

contrast.en: NOx and N₂O (nitrous oxide) are different groups of gases. N₂O is a greenhouse gas, but it is not counted in NOx.
contrast.ru: NOx и N₂O (закись азота) — разные группы газов. N₂O — парниковый газ, но в NOx он не входит.

sources.title: US EPA — Basic Information about NO₂
sources.section: Formation of NO₂; ozone, particles and acid rain

rates.title: Rates of Reaction
rates.intro: How fast a reaction goes, and the four factors that change its rate: temperature, concentration, surface area and catalyst.

definition.title: What is the rate of reaction?
definition.body: **Rate of reaction** is the change in the amount (or concentration) of a reactant or product per unit time. Average rate = change in amount ÷ time taken. Always give the units, for example mol/(dm³·s) for concentration or cm³/s for gas volume.

review.englishTerm: What is the rate of reaction?

contrast.en: Rate and the amount of product are different things. A reaction can make a lot of product slowly, or a little product quickly.
contrast.ru: Скорость и количество продукта — разные величины. Реакция может медленно дать много продукта или быстро дать мало.

collision.title: Collision theory
collision.body: Collision theory explains reaction rate through particle collisions. An **effective collision** needs energy at least equal to the activation energy, and the particles must be correctly oriented. A faster reaction needs more effective collisions per second, not just more collisions.

contrast.en: Activation energy is not the energy released by a reaction. It is the barrier particles must overcome. The enthalpy change, ΔH, is the energy released or absorbed overall.
contrast.ru: Энергия активации — это не энергия, которая выделяется в реакции. Это барьер, который должны преодолеть частицы. Изменение энтальпии (enthalpy change) ΔH показывает, сколько энергии выделяется или поглощается в целом.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.rule: Raising the temperature usually speeds up a reaction. Particles move faster, so they collide more often, and a larger fraction of them have energy at least equal to the activation energy. A rise of 10 °C does not always double the rate.
examples: Food lasts longer in a fridge, because low temperature slows the growth of bacteria.
A glow stick is brighter in warm water than in ice-cold water, because the reaction runs faster when it is warm.
temperature.tip: In a rate experiment, measure the temperature of the reacting mixture itself, not the room, and keep it constant (a water bath helps).

contrast.en: Heating does not lower the activation energy: for a given reaction, it stays the same.
contrast.ru: Нагревание не снижает энергию активации: для этой реакции она остаётся прежней.

concentration.name: Concentration (and pressure for gases)
concentration.rule: A higher reactant concentration means more particles in the same volume, so collisions happen more often and the rate increases. For gases, raising the pressure at a fixed temperature has the same effect, because it squeezes the particles closer together. The quantitative relationship is found by experiment: doubling a concentration does not always double the rate.
examples: The same mass of magnesium reacts much faster with concentrated hydrochloric acid than with dilute acid.
A glowing splint bursts into flame in pure oxygen but only stays glowing in air, where oxygen is less concentrated.
concentration.watchOut: Usually the rate is highest at the start, when reactant concentration is greatest. It slows as the reactant is used up, so do not assume one rate for the whole reaction.

contrast.en: Concentration is not the same as the amount of substance. Twice the volume of the same solution holds twice the substance, yet its concentration is the same, so the rate in mol/(dm³·s) does not change.
contrast.ru: Концентрация — это не количество вещества (amount of substance). Вдвое больший объём того же раствора содержит вдвое больше вещества, но концентрация та же, поэтому скорость в моль/(дм³·с) не меняется.

surfaceArea.name: Surface area (of solids)
surfaceArea.rule: A solid reacts at its surface. The larger the surface area, the more of its particles contact the other reactant at the same time. Grinding the same mass into powder exposes more surface, so the reaction speeds up.
examples: The same mass of marble reacts much faster with acid as powder than as lumps: the powder fizzes vigorously.
Flour dust in mills can explode, because very fine particles have a huge total surface area and burn almost at once.
surfaceArea.tip: Cutting a 1 cm cube into 1 mm cubes gives 1000 small cubes. The total surface area rises from 6 cm² to 60 cm², but the mass stays the same.

contrast.en: Powder does not raise the concentration of the acid. Concentration describes the solution, while surface area describes the solid.
contrast.ru: Порошок не повышает концентрацию кислоты. Концентрация относится к раствору, а площадь поверхности — к твёрдому веществу.

catalyst.name: Catalyst
catalyst.rule: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by providing another pathway with a lower activation energy. It takes part in intermediate steps but returns to its original form at the end, so it is not used up.
examples: MnO₂ catalyses the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) into water (H₂O) and oxygen (O₂). The reaction gives off oxygen bubbles rapidly.
Iron catalyses the Haber process: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g).
Enzymes in your body — biological catalysts (amylase, pepsin).
catalyst.tip: On an energy profile diagram, the catalysed route has a lower peak, but the start and end levels are the same, so ΔH does not change.

contrast.en: A catalyst is not a reactant or a product, so in an equation it goes above the arrow.
contrast.ru: Катализатор — не реагент и не продукт, поэтому в уравнении его пишут над стрелкой.

graphs.title: Drawing rate graphs
graphs.body: On a graph of amount against time, product curves rise and reactant curves fall. To find the rate at one moment, draw a tangent to the curve and measure its slope. For a reactant, the rate is the negative of the slope. A flat part means no further measured change: the reaction has finished or reached equilibrium.

contrast.en: Do not confuse the initial rate (the tangent at t = 0) with the average rate over the whole reaction.
contrast.ru: Не путай начальную скорость (касательная при t = 0) со средней скоростью за весь опыт.

experiments.title: Carrying out a rate experiment
experiments.body: In a rate experiment, measure a quantity that changes over time. For calcium carbonate and acid, this is the volume of CO₂ collected or the mass lost as the gas escapes. Change one factor only, keep the other conditions the same, and repeat each measurement to check your results.

contrast.en: When you time a fixed volume of gas, a shorter time means a faster rate. The rate is proportional to 1/time, not to the time itself.
contrast.ru: Если измеряешь время, за которое собирается фиксированный объём газа, то меньшее время означает большую скорость. Скорость пропорциональна 1/t, а не самому времени.

extras.intro: Extension: topics beyond the G9 list, and a more detailed look at its topics. Read these after the main topics, not instead of them.

organic.title: Organic chemistry — intro
organic.body: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, their structures and their reactions. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen. Alkanes without a ring have the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkenes with one C=C double bond have CₙH₂ₙ. A functional group is a group of atoms that determines a compound's characteristic reactions: –OH in alcohols and –COOH in carboxylic acids.

contrast.en: Not every carbon compound is organic. Carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and carbonates are classed as inorganic.
contrast.ru: Не каждое соединение углерода — органическое. Оксиды углерода (CO, CO₂) и карбонаты (carbonates) относят к неорганическим (inorganic).

model.en: C₃H₆ can be propene, an alkene with a C=C double bond, or cyclopropane, a ring of three carbon atoms with no double bond. Both fit the general formula CₙH₂ₙ, so the formula alone does not prove that a compound is an alkene.
model.ru: Формуле C₃H₆ отвечают пропен (алкен с двойной связью C=C) и циклопропан (кольцо из трёх атомов углерода без двойной связи). Оба вещества подходят под общую формулу CₙH₂ₙ, поэтому сама формула не доказывает, что перед нами алкен.

redox.title: Redox reactions
redox.body: Oxidation is the loss of electrons; reduction is the gain of electrons. The two always happen together, so the electrons lost by one substance are gained by another. A reducing agent is oxidised as it reduces another substance, and an oxidising agent is reduced. Oxidation state is a formal charge found by a set of rules. It is not always the real charge on the atom.

contrast.en: Oxygen is not always involved: in Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g), zinc is oxidised and hydrogen ions are reduced.
contrast.ru: Кислород участвует не всегда: в реакции Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g) цинк окисляется, а ионы водорода восстанавливаются.

electrochem.title: Electrochemistry
electrochem.body: An electrolytic cell uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction. Reduction happens at the cathode and oxidation at the anode, whatever the cell type. A galvanic cell uses a spontaneous redox reaction to produce electrical energy. The products formed in an electrolytic cell depend on the electrolyte, the electrodes and the conditions.

contrast.en: Do not mix up the signs. In an electrolytic cell the cathode is negative and the anode positive; in a galvanic cell the signs are reversed.
contrast.ru: Не путай знаки электродов. В электролитической ячейке катод отрицателен, а анод положителен; в гальваническом элементе знаки меняются на противоположные.

rates.title: Rates of reaction
items: Concentration: a reactant usually changes the rate only if it takes part in the slowest step, the rate-determining step.

Temperature: the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve shifts to the right and widens, while its area stays the same. If the vertical axis shows the number of particles, the area equals the total number of particles.
Surface area: a solid catalyst works on its surface. A car's catalytic converter coats a porous support with platinum, palladium and rhodium, so the catalyst has a large surface area.
Catalyst poisoning: impurities bind strongly to the catalyst's surface, so less of the surface is left for the reactants.
Light starts photochemical reactions. A mixture of H₂ and Cl₂ hardly reacts in the dark, but it can explode in bright light.

contrast.en: The main topic explains the four factors through collisions and activation energy. The extension adds that some effects depend on the mechanism, the sequence of steps in the reaction.
contrast.ru: Основная тема объясняет четыре фактора через столкновения частиц и энергию активации. Углубление добавляет, что эффект некоторых факторов зависит от механизма (mechanism), то есть от последовательности стадий реакции.

equilibrium.title: Dynamic equilibrium — intro
equilibrium.body: In a closed system, dynamic equilibrium is reached when the forward and reverse reactions run at equal rates. The concentrations then stay constant.

contrast.en: Equilibrium does not mean that reactant and product concentrations are equal.
contrast.ru: Равновесие не значит, что концентрации реагентов и продуктов равны.

atomsPeriodic.title: Atomic Structure & Periodic Table
atomsPeriodic.intro: How atoms are built, what isotopes are, how electrons are arranged in shells, and how the periodic table is organised.

atomicStructure.title: Atomic structure
atomicStructure.body: An atom has a tiny, positively charged nucleus. Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus. Mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons. Electrons occupy energy levels (shells) around the nucleus. A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons. For example, oxygen-16 has Z = 8 and A = 16: its nucleus holds 8 protons and 8 neutrons, and the neutral atom has 8 electrons.

contrast.en: Electrons add almost no mass: one electron is about 1836 times less massive than a proton. So mass number A does not count electrons, and an ion has almost the same mass as its atom.
contrast.ru: Электроны почти не дают массы: один электрон примерно в 1836 раз легче протона. Поэтому электроны не входят в массовое число A, и масса иона почти равна массе атома.

sources.section: РЭШ, 8 класс, урок 26 «Строение атома. Состав атомных ядер. Изотопы», раздел «Строение атома». Не открыт из среды, проверить вручную.

isotopes.title: Isotopes
isotopes.body: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. They therefore have the same atomic number (Z) but different mass numbers (A). Neutral atoms of all isotopes of an element have the same number of electrons, so isotopes react in almost the same way. Properties that depend on mass, such as density, differ slightly.

contrast.en: Equal mass numbers do not mean the same element: carbon-14 and nitrogen-14 both have A = 14, but their Z values are 6 and 7.
contrast.ru: Одинаковое массовое число ещё не значит, что это один элемент: у углерода-14 и азота-14 A = 14, а Z — 6 и 7 соответственно.

model.en: For hydrogen the mass difference is large: deuterium (hydrogen-2) is about twice as heavy as hydrogen-1, so reactions in which a bond to deuterium breaks can run noticeably slower.
model.ru: У водорода разница в массе велика: дейтерий (deuterium, водород-2) примерно вдвое тяжелее обычного водорода (водород-1). Поэтому реакции, в которых рвётся связь с дейтерием, могут идти заметно медленнее.

label.ru: Относительная атомная масса (relative atomic mass) Ar

detail.en: The weighted average mass of an atom of the element, compared with 1/12 of the mass of an atom of carbon-12. Isotopes are weighted by their natural abundance. For carbon it is about 12.01.
detail.ru: Средняя масса атома элемента с учётом долей изотопов в природе по сравнению с 1/12 массы атома углерода-12. Для углерода это около 12,01.

caption.en: Both neutral atoms have six electrons. A is always a whole number, but Ar usually is not.
caption.ru: У обоих нейтральных атомов по шесть электронов. Массовое число A всегда целое, а Ar обычно нецелое.

electronConfig.title: Electron configuration
electronConfig.body: An electron configuration shows how many electrons sit in each shell of an atom. A shell holds at most 2n² electrons, where n is the shell number. For example, a neutral sodium atom in its ground state (lowest energy) has the configuration 2, 8, 1, and calcium has 2, 8, 8, 2.

contrast.en: Sodium is in period 3 because it has 3 shells, and in group 1 because it has 1 outer electron.
contrast.ru: Натрий стоит в периоде 3, потому что у него 3 слоя, и в группе 1, потому что у него один внешний электрон.

model.en: The 2, 8, 8, 2 pattern does not carry past calcium.

periodicTable.title: Reading the periodic table
periodicTable.body: An element is a substance made of one kind of atom. The periodic table lists elements in order of increasing atomic number, not relative atomic mass. Each row is a period and each column is a group. IUPAC numbers the groups from 1 to 18. Group 1 holds the alkali metals, apart from hydrogen. Group 17 holds the halogens, and group 18 holds the noble gases. The old school labels VIIA and 0 (VIIIA) mean groups 17 and 18. Most elements are metals. Metals lie to the left of a stepped line that runs from boron to astatine; non-metals lie to its right.

contrast.en: The old label Group 7 (VIIA) means halogens, but IUPAC group 7 is manganese, a transition metal. Halogens are group 17 in IUPAC numbering.
contrast.ru: В старом обозначении «группа 7» (VIIA) — галогены, а по ИЮПАК в группе 7 — марганец, переходный металл (transition metal). Галогены в нумерации ИЮПАК — группа 17.

model.en: So argon (relative atomic mass 39.95) comes before potassium (relative atomic mass 39.10), even though argon’s relative atomic mass is larger.
model.ru: Поэтому аргон (относительная атомная масса 39,95) стоит раньше калия (относительная атомная масса 39,10), хотя его относительная атомная масса больше.

trends.title: How properties change down a group
trends.body: These changes come from nuclear charge, shielding by inner electrons and the number of shells. Alkali metals become more reactive down group 1. The outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is lost more easily. Halogens become less oxidising down group 17, because the larger atom attracts an extra electron less strongly.

review.englishTerm: How properties change down a group

contrast.en: Reactivity of alkali metals increases down group 1, but their melting points decrease. A trend in one property does not predict another.
contrast.ru: Реакционная способность щелочных металлов растёт вниз по группе 1, а температура плавления падает. Закономерность для одного свойства не позволяет предсказать другое.

model.en: These group patterns apply to main-group elements. Do not apply them to transition metals (groups 3–12), which can have several oxidation states.
model.ru: Эти закономерности относятся к элементам главных групп (main-group elements). Не переноси их на переходные металлы (transition metals, группы 3–12): они могут иметь несколько степеней окисления.

bonding.title: Bonding
bonding.intro: Atoms join by ionic, covalent or metallic bonding. The type of bonding helps explain why a substance has its properties.

ionic.title: Ionic bonding
ionic.body: Ionic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions. It usually forms between a metal and a non-metal. In sodium chloride, a sodium atom loses one electron and a chlorine atom gains it, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. Electron transfer explains how the ions form, but the bond itself is the attraction between them, not the transfer. The attraction acts in all directions, so the ions form a regular three-dimensional lattice.

contrast.en: Do not confuse ionic and covalent bonds. In an ionic bond, one atom gives electrons to another, forming ions. In a covalent bond, atoms share electron pairs.
contrast.ru: Не путай ионную и ковалентную связь: при ионной связи один атом отдаёт электроны другому, а при ковалентной атомы делят общую электронную пару.

sources.title: РЭШ, 8 кл., урок 29 «Электроотрицательность химических элементов. Ионная связь» (не открыт из среды; проверить вручную, Q11.5)
sources.section: Урок 29: Электроотрицательность химических элементов. Ионная связь

covalent.title: Covalent bonding
covalent.body: A covalent bond is the attraction of a shared pair of electrons to the nuclei of two atoms. Atoms can share one or more pairs: in hydrogen, H₂, the two atoms share one pair, and in oxygen, O₂, they share two pairs. If the atoms attract the shared pair equally, the bond is non-polar, as in H₂ and O₂. If one atom attracts it more strongly, as in HCl, the bond is polar. Covalent substances form either simple molecular or giant covalent structures.

contrast.en: A covalent bond holds atoms together inside a molecule. Intermolecular forces are much weaker: boiling water breaks them, but the O–H bonds inside each H₂O molecule stay intact.
contrast.ru: Ковалентная связь удерживает атомы внутри молекулы. Межмолекулярные взаимодействия (intermolecular forces) намного слабее: при кипении воды они разрываются, а связи O–H внутри молекул H₂O остаются целыми.

sources.title: РЭШ, 8 кл., урок 30 «Ковалентная химическая связь. Полярная и неполярная ковалентная связь» (не открыт из среды; проверить вручную, Q11.5)
sources.section: Урок 30: Ковалентная химическая связь. Полярная и неполярная ковалентная связь

metallic.title: Metallic bonding
metallic.body: Metallic bonding is the attraction between positive metal ions (cations) and delocalised electrons that move freely through the whole metal. Because the bonding is not directional, layers of ions can slide past each other without breaking the bonds, so metals can be bent and hammered into shape.

contrast.en: In a metal, outer electrons belong to the whole structure, not to a pair of atoms as in a covalent bond. So they are not transferred to particular atoms, as happens in an ionic bond.
contrast.ru: В металле внешние электроны принадлежат всей структуре, а не одной паре атомов, как в ковалентной связи. Поэтому они не переходят к отдельным атомам, как при ионной связи.

sources.section: Урок 31: Металлическая связь и кристаллические решётки

items.ionic: Ionic solids: ions in a regular, three-dimensional lattice.
items.simpleCovalent: Simple molecular substances: separate molecules, each a group of atoms joined by covalent bonds.
items.giantCovalent: Giant covalent substances, such as diamond and SiO₂: atoms bonded into one extended structure, usually with a very high melting point.
items.metallic: Metals: positive ions in a cloud of delocalised electrons, so they conduct heat and electricity, and can be shaped.

ionic.name: Ionic lattice
ionic.rule: Each ion is pulled by several oppositely charged neighbours at once, so the lattice is strong. Melting means overcoming many of these strong attractions, which needs a lot of energy, so the melting point is high. When the substance melts or dissolves, the ions can move, so the liquid or solution conducts.
examples: NaCl (table salt) melts at 801 °C; water melts at 0 °C.
MgO (magnesium oxide) melts at about 2850 °C. Its ions carry charges of 2+ and 2−, and the small Mg²⁺ ion attracts the O²⁻ ions strongly.
CaF₂ (fluorite) is an ionic crystal used in some optical lenses, because it transmits ultraviolet light well.
MgCl₂ (magnesium chloride): each Mg atom gives up two electrons and each Cl atom takes one, so the formula has one Mg²⁺ ion for every two Cl⁻ ions.
ionic.tip: When you compare two ionic solids, consider ion charges, ion sizes and structure together. Charge alone does not predict the melting point.

contrast.en: Ionic crystals are brittle, but metals are malleable. When an ionic lattice shifts, ions of like charge are brought side by side, repel each other, and the crystal shatters. In a metal, the layers slide while the ions stay attracted to the delocalised electrons.
contrast.ru: Вещества с ионной кристаллической решёткой хрупкие, а металлы ковкие. При сдвиге слоёв ионной кристаллической решётки одноимённые ионы оказываются рядом, отталкиваются, и кристалл раскалывается. В металле слои скользят, а ионы остаются притянутыми к делокализованным электронам (delocalised electrons).

sources.title: РЭШ, 8 кл., урок 34 «Повторение и обобщение: строение атома, строение вещества, химическая связь» (не открыт из среды; проверить вручную, Q11.5)
sources.section: Урок 34: Повторение и обобщение: строение вещества, химическая связь

simpleCovalent.name: Simple molecular structure
simpleCovalent.rule: Melting or boiling only separates the molecules from one another. The intermolecular forces between them are weak, so little energy is needed, and these substances melt and boil at low temperatures.
examples: At atmospheric pressure, dry ice (solid CO₂) sublimes at about −78 °C. It turns straight into gas and never becomes a liquid.
Iodine (I₂) is a solid at room temperature. Weak forces act between its molecules, so it melts at about 114 °C.
simpleCovalent.tip: Compare the forces between molecules, not only their mass: methane (CH₄, 16 g/mol) boils at −162 °C, while water (H₂O, 18 g/mol) boils at 100 °C.

contrast.en: Pure hydrogen chloride, a molecular substance, does not conduct electricity. Its solution does, because the HCl molecules split into H⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in water.
contrast.ru: Чистый хлороводород, молекулярное вещество, ток не проводит. Его раствор проводит, потому что в воде молекулы HCl распадаются на ионы H⁺ и Cl⁻.

giantCovalent.name: Giant covalent (macromolecular)
giantCovalent.rule: In diamond each bond points in a fixed direction, so the atoms cannot slide past one another: the crystal breaks rather than bends. Melting requires breaking many of these strong covalent bonds throughout the crystal, which takes a great deal of energy.
examples: Quartz, the main part of sand, is SiO₂: each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms, and each oxygen atom to two silicon atoms. It melts at about 1700 °C.
Diamond has a hardness of 10 on the Mohs scale, the highest value on that scale. Graphite, also pure carbon, has a hardness of only 1–2.
giantCovalent.watchOut: Do not confuse allotropes with isotopes. Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon: both contain only carbon atoms, but the atoms are arranged differently. Isotopes of an element have different numbers of neutrons.

contrast.en: A very high melting point does not make a substance unreactive. When heated strongly in air, diamond burns to form carbon dioxide.
contrast.ru: Очень высокая температура плавления не делает вещество химически инертным. При сильном нагреве на воздухе алмаз сгорает с образованием углекислого газа (CO₂).

sources.title: РЭШ, 8 кл., урок 34 «Повторение и обобщение: строение атома, строение вещества, химическая связь» (не открыт из среды; проверить вручную, Q11.5)

metallic.name: Metallic lattice
metallic.rule: Generally, the more outer electrons each metal atom contributes to the delocalised electrons, the more tightly the positive ions are held. Holding the ions more tightly takes more energy to melt the metal, so its melting point is usually higher. The size of the ions also affects the melting point.
examples: Magnesium, with two delocalised electrons per atom, melts at 650 °C. Sodium, with one per atom, melts at 98 °C.
Copper conducts electricity better than any metal except silver, so it is used in electrical wiring.
Gold is so malleable that it can be hammered into very thin leaf.
Aluminium has a low density (2.7 g/cm³) and conducts electricity well, so it is used in overhead power cables.
Brass (copper and zinc) and steel (iron and carbon) are alloys, and both are harder than the pure metals. Atoms of different sizes disturb the layers, so the layers slide less easily.

contrast.en: An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, such as carbon in steel, so its composition can vary: brass can contain more or less zinc. A compound has a fixed composition.
contrast.ru: Сплав — смесь (mixture) металла с другими элементами, например углеродом в стали, поэтому состав может меняться: в латуни можно взять больше или меньше цинка. Сложное вещество (compound) имеет постоянный состав.

reactions.title: Reactions & Equations
reactions.intro: Types of chemical reactions and how to balance equations correctly.

combination.name: Combination (synthesis)
combination.rule: A combination reaction forms a single product substance from two or more reactant substances. A schematic form is A + B → AB; an actual equation must use correct formulae and balanced coefficients. This classification can overlap with others, such as oxidation.
examples: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) — hydrogen burns in oxygen
CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) — quicklime + water
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g) — Haber process
combination.tip: Reaction classification does not determine the sign of ΔH; consider the full energy balance.

contrast.en: Coefficients change numbers of particles; changing a formula’s subscripts changes the substance. Atoms and total charge must balance.
contrast.ru: Коэффициенты меняют числа частиц; изменение индексов формулы меняет вещество. Числа атомов и общий заряд должны сохраняться.

decomposition.name: Decomposition
decomposition.rule: A decomposition reaction converts one compound into two or more product substances. It may be driven by heat, light or electricity. For example, CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ on heating; decomposition changes chemical identity rather than merely separating a mixture.
examples: 2H₂O₂(aq) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g) — peroxide with MnO₂ catalyst
CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g) — limestone heated
2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) — electrolysis of water
decomposition.tip: Thermal decomposition of carbonates is a classic G9 example.

displacement.name: Single displacement
displacement.rule: A displacement reaction occurs when one element replaces another in a compound. For example, zinc reduces copper ions: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu. Reactivity-series predictions apply under specified conditions; competing reactions and protective surface films can affect what is observed.
examples: Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s) — blue colour fades, brown copper deposits
Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g) — magnesium 'fizzes'
displacement.watchOut: A less reactive metal is not predicted to displace a more reactive metal from its salt in the simple school model. This does not rule out other reactions in a particular system.

doubleDisplacement.name: Double displacement (precipitation)
doubleDisplacement.rule: In a double-displacement reaction, ions exchange partners. A precipitation reaction is the case where dissolved ions form an insoluble solid, for example Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s). Ion exchange does not always produce a precipitate; water or gas formation can also drive reactions.
examples: AgNO₃(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s)↓ + NaNO₃(aq) — white precipitate of silver chloride
Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s)↓ + 2KNO₃(aq) — bright yellow precipitate
doubleDisplacement.tip: Memorise common insoluble compounds: AgCl, BaSO₄, CaCO₃, PbI₂. They appear as the precipitate.

combustion.name: Combustion
combustion.rule: Combustion is an exothermic reaction of a fuel with an oxidant, usually oxygen in this course. Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon forms CO₂ and H₂O. Inadequate oxygen or mixing can cause incomplete combustion, producing CO and/or soot as well as other products.
examples: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g) — methane gas
2C₈H₁₈(l) + 25O₂(g) → 16CO₂(g) + 18H₂O(g) — petrol (octane)
combustion.watchOut: Complete combustion needs an adequate oxygen supply and effective mixing; flame colour alone is not a quantitative gas analysis.

neutralisation.name: Neutralisation
neutralisation.rule: Neutralisation is reaction between an acid and a base. For a strong acid and hydroxide alkali in dilute water, the net equation is H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l), with heat released. Other acid–base reactions can have different products; the final solution is not automatically pH 7.
examples: HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l)
H₂SO₄(aq) + 2KOH(aq) → K₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l)
2HNO₃(aq) + Mg(OH)₂(s) → Mg(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l)
neutralisation.tip: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O applies to strong aqueous acid with hydroxide alkali; weak acids require different ionic notation.

contrast.en: Strength describes the extent of ionisation or reaction with water; concentration describes amount per volume. They are different quantities.
contrast.ru: Сила характеризует полноту ионизации или реакции с водой; концентрация — количество на объём. Это разные характеристики.

balancing.body: A balanced equation has equal numbers of atoms of each element on both sides and conserves charge when ions are shown. Adjust coefficients multiplying whole formulae; changing subscripts changes the substances. For example, 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.

stateSymbols.body: State symbols specify the physical state under the reaction conditions: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas and (aq) dissolved in water. stoichiometry.title: Stoichiometry
stoichiometry.intro: Quantitative chemistry — how much of each substance reacts.

moles.title: The mole
moles.body: The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance. One mole contains exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ specified particles, such as atoms, molecules or ions. Reactions combine particles in fixed ratios, so chemists work with amounts of substance in moles. For a pure substance, divide the mass by the molar mass to find the amount.

contrast.en: A mole is not a unit of mass: one mole of magnesium atoms has a mass of about 24 g, and one mole of sulfur atoms has a mass of about 32 g.
contrast.ru: Моль — не единица массы: 1 моль атомов магния имеет массу около 24 г, а 1 моль атомов серы — около 32 г.

molarMass.title: Molar mass
molarMass.body: Molar mass (M) is the mass of one mole of a substance, usually in g/mol. To find a compound's molar mass, add the relative atomic masses of all its atoms, counting the subscripts. For example, M(H₂SO₄) = 2 × 1 + 32 + 4 × 16 = 98 g/mol.

contrast.en: Relative formula mass (Mr) has no unit, but molar mass (M) is in g/mol. For water, Mr = 18 and M = 18 g/mol: the numbers match, but Mr is a ratio, not a mass per mole.
contrast.ru: Относительная молекулярная (формульная) масса Mr (relative formula mass) не имеет единицы, а молярная масса M указывается в г/моль. Для воды Mr = 18 и M = 18 г/моль: числа совпадают, но Mr — это отношение, а не масса одного моля.

caption.en: a and b are coefficients in the balanced equation: a for the reactant, b for the product. If amounts of two reactants are given, first find the limiting reactant.
caption.ru: a и b — коэффициенты уравнения: a относится к реагенту, b к продукту. Если даны количества вещества двух реагентов, сначала найди вещество в недостатке.

limiting.title: Limiting reactant
limiting.body: The limiting reactant is the one that runs out first. It sets the maximum possible amount of product. To find it, divide the amount of each reactant by its coefficient. The smallest result identifies the limiting reactant, assuming the reaction goes to completion.

contrast.en: The limiting reactant does not always leave an excess. If the amounts are in the same ratio as the coefficients, both reactants run out together. For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 0.40 mol H₂ and 0.20 mol O₂ react with nothing left over.
contrast.ru: Вещество в недостатке не всегда означает, что другой реагент взят в избытке. Если количества вещества реагентов относятся друг к другу так же, как коэффициенты, оба реагента заканчиваются одновременно. Для 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O смесь из 0,40 моль H₂ и 0,20 моль O₂ прореагирует без остатка.

percentYield.title: Percentage yield
percentYield.body: Percentage yield is the actual mass of product as a percentage of the theoretical mass. Use the same unit for both masses, such as grams. The theoretical mass is calculated from the limiting reactant. A yield above 100% usually means impurities or retained solvent, or a mistake in the measurement or calculation.

contrast.en: Divide by the theoretical mass of product, not by the mass of reactant you started with. For 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO with 4.8 g of magnesium, the theoretical mass of MgO is 8.0 g. If 6.4 g is obtained, the yield is 6.4/8.0 × 100 = 80%. Dividing by 4.8 g gives a wrong 133%.
contrast.ru: Дели на теоретическую массу продукта, а не на массу взятого реагента. В реакции 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO из 4,8 г магния теоретическая масса MgO равна 8,0 г. Если получено 6,4 г, выход равен 6,4/8,0 × 100 = 80 %. Деление на 4,8 г даёт неверные 133 %.

acidsBases.title: Acids, Bases & Salts
acidsBases.intro: pH scale, indicators, and key reactions of acids.

acid.name: Acid
acid.rule: In the Brønsted–Lowry model, an acid donates H⁺ to another species. In water, an acid increases hydronium, H₃O⁺, often written H⁺(aq). Acid strength describes the extent of ionisation in a given solvent; concentration describes how much acid is present per volume.
examples: HCl (hydrochloric acid) — stomach acid
H₂SO₄ (sulfuric acid) — car batteries
HNO₃ (nitric acid) — fertilisers
CH₃COOH (ethanoic / acetic acid) — vinegar (weak)
acid.tip: Strong acids fully ionise in water (HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻). Weak acids only partly ionise (CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺).

contrast.en: Strength describes the extent of ionisation or reaction with water; concentration describes amount per volume. They are different quantities.
contrast.ru: Сила характеризует полноту ионизации или реакции с водой; концентрация — количество на объём. Это разные характеристики.

base.name: Base
base.rule: In the Brønsted–Lowry model, a base accepts H⁺. Hydroxide ions, carbonate ions and ammonia can act as bases. School classifications also call many metal oxides basic because they react with acids. A base need not be soluble and its reaction need not produce water.
examples: CuO (copper oxide) — black solid that reacts with acid to give blue solution
MgO (magnesium oxide) — white powder
CaCO₃ (calcium carbonate) — chalk, limestone
base.tip: English school alkali means a soluble base; Russian school щёлочь usually means a soluble metal hydroxide. CuO is classed as a basic oxide in Russian inorganic nomenclature.

alkali.name: Alkali
alkali.rule: An alkali is a water-soluble base that produces an alkaline aqueous solution with excess OH⁻ over H₃O⁺. Sodium hydroxide releases OH⁻ on dissolving; ammonia forms some OH⁻ by reacting with water. Thus an alkali need not contain hydroxide ions before dissolution.

energy.title: Energy Changes
energy.intro: Chemical reactions usually release or absorb energy, mostly as heat. Here you will compare exothermic and endothermic reactions, read energy profile diagrams and calculate heat changes from bond energies and from temperature data.

exothermic.name: Exothermic reactions
exothermic.rule: An exothermic reaction transfers heat from the reacting system to its surroundings. Enthalpy (H) is the heat content of a system at constant pressure. The products have less enthalpy than the reactants, so ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants) < 0.
examples: Burning methane: methane reacts with oxygen to give carbon dioxide and liquid water. At 298 K and 100 kPa, ΔH ≈ −890 kJ mol⁻¹ of methane.
Neutralisation of a dilute strong acid by a strong alkali: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l). ΔH ≈ −57 kJ mol⁻¹ of water formed.
Aerobic respiration in cells: glucose reacts with oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water. ΔH ≈ −2800 kJ mol⁻¹ of glucose. Cells use part of this energy for life processes.

Hand warmers: iron oxidises with oxygen from the air, 4Fe(s) + 3O₂(g) → 2Fe₂O₃(s). The reaction releases heat. The iron is used as a fine powder: small particles have a large surface, so the reaction runs faster, but the heat released per mole stays the same.
Self-heating coffee cans: calcium oxide reacts with water, CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(s). The heat released warms the drink.
exothermic.tip: Do not drop the minus sign. Write ΔH = −57 kJ mol⁻¹, not 57 kJ mol⁻¹: the sign shows the direction of the heat flow, and the number shows how much heat moves.

contrast.en: An exothermic reaction is not always combustion. Burning is only one example; neutralisation and self-heating cans release heat with no flame.
contrast.ru: Экзотермическая реакция — не обязательно горение. Горение — лишь один пример; нейтрализация и самонагревающиеся банки выделяют теплоту без пламени.

endothermic.name: Endothermic reactions
endothermic.rule: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings. Its products have more enthalpy than its reactants, so ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants) > 0.
examples: Heating limestone (calcium carbonate): CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g). ΔH ≈ +178 kJ mol⁻¹, so heat must be supplied.
Dissolving ammonium nitrate cools the water: NH₄NO₃(s) → NH₄⁺(aq) + NO₃⁻(aq). ΔH ≈ +26 kJ mol⁻¹, so the water loses heat.
endothermic.watchOut: Not every energy input is heat. Photosynthesis is endothermic (ΔH > 0), but its energy comes from light, which is stored in the glucose it makes.

contrast.en: Temperature is not the same as heat. A falling temperature shows that the surroundings gave heat to the reaction, but it does not measure how much energy moved.
contrast.ru: Температура — не то же, что теплота. Понижение температуры показывает, что среда отдала реакции теплоту, но не показывает, сколько энергии перешло.

profiles.title: Energy profile diagrams
profiles.body: An energy profile diagram shows enthalpy (H) against reaction progress. The reactants and the products sit at two levels. The change in level from reactants to products is ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants). The activation energy (Eₐ) is the rise from the reactants to the peak, which is the transition state. A real reaction can have several steps and several peaks; this diagram shows one.

bondEnergies.title: Bond energies
bondEnergies.body: Bonds break in the reactants and form in the products, so the two contributions enter ΔH with opposite signs. Estimate ΔH as the sum of the bond energies broken minus the sum of the bond energies formed. Tabulated bond energies are mean values for bonds in gaseous molecules, so the result is an estimate: count every bond in the equation.

contrast.en: A bond energy is always a positive number: it is the energy needed to break one mole of that bond. The minus sign in ΔH comes from the subtraction, not from the table.
contrast.ru: Энергия связи всегда положительна: это энергия, которую нужно затратить, чтобы разорвать один моль таких связей. Минус в ΔH появляется при вычитании, а не в таблице.

calorimetry.title: Calorimetry
calorimetry.body:
Calorimetry finds heat from a temperature change. A solution of mass m (kg) that warms by ΔT (°C) gains q = mcΔT joules, where c is its specific heat capacity (J/(kg·K)). The reaction gives off the same amount of heat. Divide by 1000 and by n, the moles of reactant used, to get ΔH ≈ −mcΔT/(1000n) in kJ mol⁻¹.

Example: 0.050 kg of solution warms by 2.5 °C, and 0.025 mol of reactant reacts: ΔH ≈ −(0.050 × 4180 × 2.5)/(1000 × 0.025) ≈ −20.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

contrast.en: The sign of q(solution) is not the sign of ΔH: if the solution warms, q is positive, but ΔH of the reaction is negative.
contrast.ru: Знак Q раствора — не знак ΔH реакции: если раствор нагрелся, Q(раствора) > 0, а ΔH реакции отрицательна.

model.en: The formula assumes that no heat is lost to the air and that the cup absorbs no heat. For dilute aqueous solutions, use c = 4180 J/(kg·K) and take 1 cm³ of solution as 1 g, so 1 dm³ is 1 kg.
